free_tier.stated: Redis Free: 250 MB max data, 10 GB bandwidth/month, 1 database. Vector Free: 1 GB total data, 200M vectors x dims. QStash Free: 1,000 messages/day, 50 GB bandwidth, 1 MB message.

retention.stated: Unclaimed ephemeral DBs deleted after 3 days.

egress.terms: Redis Free caps bandwidth at 10 GB/month with max data 250 MB — a 40x fetch amplification before the egress meter binds. Vector Free: bandwidth free/unmetered, storage 1 GB is the wall.

tooling: Redis protocol (any redis client), REST API for all three products, `@upstash/redis` SDK; QStash is HTTP-only
chaining: One free database per account on Redis Free ('Max databases | 1') — no per-project multiplication. BUT: `GET https://upstash.com/start-redis` mints a keyless, unauthenticated free Redis with no signup (deleted after 3 days unless claimed); claimed ones become normal free DBs. Vector's 1 GB with 1 MB per vector and 200M vectors is the better storage shape: unlimited vector COUNT, only total bytes capped.
limits_note: 250 MB is tiny. 1 database per account. QStash 1 MB max message size makes it useless as storage. Request size 10 MB (upgradeable). Unclaimed ephemeral DBs deleted after 3 days.
reliability_note: Ephemeral DBs (unclaimed) hard-delete at 3 days — data vanishes by design. Claimed free DBs are durable.

evidence.proved: probe: GET -> 200, documents zero-signup POST with Idempotency-Key; 'Databases live for 3 days unless claimed'
